source: the raw records of the runners of GitHub, judged again with the catalog after the calibration of the propagation

cells.name: iptables, the propagation of a deletion, preStop 10 s

prediction.text: This cell is a calibration. A preStop sleep of 10 s keeps the pod open while the deletion propagates, thus no request fails. Each node gives its propagation: the time from the deletion to the first poll of its rules without the pod.

cells.why: The calibration measured the propagation in each of the 11 counted runs.

cells.name: iptables, pod deletion, the design's hold of 2 s

prediction.text: The algebra predicts that no request fails.

cells.why: Each of the 11 counted runs agrees with the prediction. The median run had 0 failed requests.

cells.name: iptables, pod deletion, no hold and no preStop

prediction.text: The algebra predicts that each failed request starts in a window. The window opens at the stop of the intake, and it closes 0 s to 105 ms after the deletion of the pod. A request after the window can also fail with a timeout, on a port that a reset of the same client closed up to 10 s before it: the CLOSE entry of that reset keeps its NAT to the pod.

cells.why: Each of the 11 counted runs agrees with the prediction. The median run had 2 failed requests. The counted runs had 0 to 5 failed requests.
